pro_course_detail.title: Conversation practice
pro_course_detail.description:
Have you tried all the apps and textbooks but still have problems with everyday conversations in English?

It's time to change your focus.
Do you feel "stuck" with your English? Maybe you've almost given up because...

-You're overwhelmed with the amount of vocabulary (phrasal verbs, idioms, and expressions) you need to learn and don't know where to begin.
-You feel like you translate in your head instead of thinking in English.
-You don't feel comfortable speaking with English speakers and you often have to ask them to repeat themselves.
-Despite all your efforts, your English isn't getting any better.

As a certified English teacher who specializes in teaching intermediate level students, I'm here to tell you that it's not your fault. You just need something real!

You'll learn how to...

*Understand a variety of different American English speakers when they talk about real-world situations. (So you can stop asking them to repeat themselves or pretending like you understood them when you actually didn't!)

*Correctly use and remember 100s of new words, expressions, idioms, and phrasal verbs.
(So your real personality can shine when you're having conversations in English.)

*Expand your vocabulary on different topics by hearing new words in context.
(Without translating words in your brain!)

*Pronounce things more naturally when speaking in English.
(So you can feel confident and understood.)

pro_course_detail.description:
Please Note: I don't offer structured German lessons for beginners. 

My goal is to help self-study students or those already taking some type of formal instruction.

I especially welcome learners having difficulty with German grammar. When I first started teaching myself, I realized I didn't understand the German grammatical terms and concepts. Then it dawned on me that I didn't really understand them in my native language, English, either. So I had to stop and learn all that before I could go any further. If you, like me, picked up your native language without thinking much about its grammar, I can help you learn what you need to know to understand German grammar.

Of course, understanding German grammar and being able to use it are two different things. If your goal is to speak German spontaneously and correctly, certain concepts and information must be internalized. There are various methods for accomplishing this, and the right way is the one that works best for you. As a self-learner, I tried virtually every resource I could get my hands on, so I can give you lots of suggestions.

In any case, I'll give you the opportunity to speak German as much as possible, either as a means of putting grammatical concepts into practice, or just for the fun of it.
